chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'What is obligatory upon the one who performs Hajj on behalf of a man?' He said, 'He should name him in the places and the stations.'
ai.seo_question: What must a person do when performing Hajj on behalf of someone else?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies the procedural validity of Hajj al-Tamattu' or Hajj al-Qiran when performed on behalf of another (Hajj 'an al-Akhar), emphasizing that the performer must explicitly invoke the name of the principal during the critical stations (mawaqit) and positions (mawatin). In Shia jurisprudence, this explicit mention (tasmiyah) is considered a condition for the validity of the ritual, ensuring the spiritual merit is correctly attributed to the deceased or absent person. This practice underscores the Shia view of Hajj as a personal obligation that can be delegated, provided the specific intent and identification are maintained throughout the key rites.
